parsed.why: No criminalisation, a 2019 statute barring gender-identity discrimination across goods and services, official sensitisation, and no documented LGBT abuses. No traveler-facing restrictions; thin data on border/facility practice keeps it short of the top band.

Cross-dressing offence struck down only in 2022, yet dress-code policing, official discrimination and strict morality enforcement persist; Article 193 still carries seven years, censorship and no LGBTQ organisation. State-targeted exposure with no working recourse.

Decriminalised, but acceptance scores near zero, a 2024 record of torture and extortion against LGBT people, legislators calling for a trans speaker to be burned alive, no protection statute, and slow state response — hostility with thin recourse.

Decriminalised in 2016 plus a 2024 hate-crime statute expressly covering gender identity, constitutional non-discrimination and freedom from torture. No documented traveler-facing exposure; only unmeasured divergence from statute tempers the score.

Criminal incitement law on gender-identity grounds, prejudice aggravation and conversion-practice ban, but enforcement is documented as inconsistent — police decline hate findings and clergy incitement goes unpunished. Protections exist yet operate unevenly across the divided territory.
